units.translation: b. νεοστασίη: instead of: she was in a state of new stories, or a pause of stories seized her and the thought of a newly occurring tale.
77a. The sense: she revered herself, seeing herself honored by Hera.
b. ἀντομένην: supplicating, entreating. Lm (P)
86. παρθένον Αἰήτεω: instead of daughter. It can also be understood thus: of the daughters of Aeetes, the one who is a virgin.

b. δολόεσσα: cunning. LgP

97-99a. 〈χαλεφθείς:〉 The sense: for being angry with me harshly he threatened that, unless I keep my hands off, while he still controls his anger, I will be deprived of him. The word ἑοῖ is not well placed. Lm (P)

b. 〈θυμόν:〉 written μῦθον. Lg

106. ῥαδινῆς: delicate. Anacreon used ῥαδινόν of swiftness (fg 165 B. III 294) 'ῥαδινοὺς πώλους'; Ibycus (fg 58 B. III 251) of the pillars that support the heaven, calling them large; Stesichorus of the vigorous (fg 53 B. III 224) 'ῥαδινοὺς δ’ ἐπέπεμπον ἄκοντας'.
4 λέγων in W and Wil. ad l. : -ει in L : differently in P
5 ἐπέπ- in L : ἔπ- in PH
107. παραβλήδην: instead of comparing with what has been said; for it should not be understood as deceiving. Palamedes [used it] from retort or misleadingly, but here from reply.

7 Et. Gen. (AB) παραβλήδην: . . . it is (in AB after λόγοις is read ἔστι, here σημαίνει, corrected by W) but in Apollonius instead of comparing and consoling with words, and in Homer (Δ 6) speaking deceitfully.
110. 〈μεταλλήξει:〉 will change. GgSm
10 here the glossator perhaps read μεταλλάξει
112. παλίσσυτοι: rushing back. LgP

114-17a. ἀπάνευθε Διός: the phrase is ambiguous. For it means 'apart from Zeus' without Zeus, which is more likely; or the word 'others' is missing, so that it would be: apart from the others in the garden of Zeus. Homer (Υ 234) says that Ganymede was not snatched by Zeus, but by the gods — 'τόν καὶ ἀνηρείψαντο θεοί' —, and not because of love and desire, but so that he might 'pour wine for Zeus'.
13 ἢ λείπει in F : ἢ συνυπακουστεόν in P : λείπει δὲ in L
16 the words τόν καὶ ἀν. θεοί, which are read at the end of the scholium, W transposed here; πόθον in HF : πόθος in L : πάθος in A : omitted in P

b. [βῆ δὲ διὲκ μεγάροιο:] through these verses he paraphrases what was said by Ibycus in the places where he spoke about the abduction of Ganymede in the Ode to Gorgias (fg 30 B. III 247); and he adds about Eos, how she snatched Tithonus. LmP
